Food:
This is the kind of Italian place that does big, familiar dishes exactly the way you want them done. The chicken parm was the best thing I had and the clearest reason to come back. It was rich, comforting, and actually felt worth ordering, not just like the safe choice on the menu. The meatballs were also excellent. Tender, full of flavor, and substantial without feeling heavy for the sake of it. The lasagna leaned more indulgent, but in a good way. It had that baked, meaty, deeply satisfying quality you want when you order lasagna at a place like this. Nothing felt phoned in. It was classic Italian food done with confidence and enough polish to make the whole meal feel worth it.

Service:
Service was professional and well paced. It felt like a place that knows how to keep a busy dining room moving without making the meal feel rushed.

Summary:
This is a very easy place to enjoy if what you want is classic Italian food done well. The chicken parm alone would be enough reason for me to go back.

text.text:
An absolute 10/10 dining experience from start to finish. The 8-course tasting menu was insanely good, hitting every high note from appetizers to desserts.
The cold squid dish with macadamia and edamame was ridiculously good—looking back, I really regret not adding the caviar upgrade, because I can only imagine how incredible it would have tasted! The fluke, halibut, and octopus courses were equally stunning, fresh, and beautifully executed.
For our main, we opted to upgrade to the A5 Wagyu instead of the duck, and it was easily the best cut of beef I have ever had. It was cooked to absolute perfection, complemented by incredible sauces and thoughtful sides. After that was the Tuna Bibimbap—the langoustine additional was sold out but I can only imagine how incredible this already incredible dish would have been.
I was initially a bit skeptical about having two full dessert courses—especially since one was billed as a palate cleanser—but they completely blew me away. Wow. Just wow. Every bite was worth it.
This team is operating at the top of their game. I’ll definitely be recommending this place to everyone I know, wish them continued success, and cannot wait to dine here again soon!

text.text:
Kochi delivers the kind of dining experience that reminds you why tasting menus can be so special. The chef’s signature menu felt like a true culinary adventure from start to finish, with eight courses that were imaginative, beautifully executed, and presented with real artistry.

The white asparagus soup was the perfect way to begin. It opened the palate beautifully and set the tone for everything that followed.

There were so many standout moments, but the halibut, duck, and bibimbap were unforgettable. If you have the option, adding the sea urchin or Scottish langoustine to the bibimbap is absolutely worth it and takes an already exceptional dish to another level. The flavors throughout the meal showed a remarkable range, moving effortlessly between bold and delicate, always feeling intentional and refined.

The service matched the food perfectly. The staff were warm, knowledgeable, and attentive in a way that elevated the entire evening. Sitting at the chef’s table is a true treat and offers a front row seat to the precision and care behind each course.

And then there are the drinks. The cocktails, wine, and soju selections round out the experience beautifully and are clearly curated with the same level of thought as the menu.

If you are in the mood for a truly star worthy dinner, this is a place you should not miss. I am still thinking about that duck. 😋

5 Stars + I came here on a Saturday night to celebrate my birthday and my best friend’s birthday. I was a little unsure because of the location as it is in the "Shops at Columbus Circle", which is a small mall. It is next to one of the most prestigious hotels in New York, which is the Mandarin Oriental Hotel.

All I can say is "WOW"!!! I am not sure where the last person who wrote a review is living, under a rock, but everything was spectacular.
Yes, prices are not cheap, although where can you go in New York City and not spend $35 to $50 on a fish dish? If you go to a diner and eat frozen fish, you will pay for that. Our bill with a generous tip was still more than $100 less than I thought I would have spent. I thought prices were fair, especially considering the overall experience, and the location in Manhattan by Central Park.

Bad Roman is a beautiful, chic spot. It is nice to see a restaurant that is as well staffed as they are. Our service was great, even down to the runners who kept our water glasses filled, tables cleaned and wiped down and provided fresh silverware with every course.

From the minute we walked in I knew it was going to be great night. There were two people at the host station who greeted us with a smile, our hostess asked if our entire party was here, and was ok with some of them being a few minutes late, as they were looking for parking. They also asked if we were celebrating anything and we informed them it was for both our birthdays.

Once everyone was here, we were seated. My friend and I were handed an envelope. In it was a nicely written birthday card for each of us. I thought that was a nice touch!

The manager Isaac came over to thank us for coming and said something that will stay with me for a lifetime when thinking about business and restaurants in general. He said "Thank you for coming and for choosing us. You could have gone anywhere to celebrate your birthday and out of all the restaurants in NYC, you choose us". What that tells me is that he and the restaurant do not take us for granted. We were not a number, and the rest of the night proved that.

The restaurant is hip and modern; there is a beautiful bar as you walk in. The bathrooms were chic and clean. The tables were spaced out, and you can breathe, you are not on top of each other. As mentioned earlier, they are well staffed and everyone was great. Hat's off to Isaac who really made the night special. He came over several times and each conversation was meaningful. It was not idle conversation, we spoke for a few minutes about food, customer service, and you could see his passion for the customer.

Our waiter Roosevelt was also great; he made sure everything was perfect. When asked, he shared his opinion on his favorite dish as did Isaac when we were torn on the selection. I am sure both dishes would have been great although each recommendation was spot on.

Now to the food. We did not have a bad dish. Portions were satisfying, with great flavor and each was nicely presented. Here are some must have dishes. For appetizers, the Babka, Pepperoni cups, the Filet Mignon meatballs which can be a side dish or appetizer, the Black Truffle Ricotta, and the Peekytoe Crab Luigi, which has an amazing presentation. Favorite dessert was the Lemon Tartuffe Cheesecake, and the chocolate cake with gelato. Favorite entrees if we had to pick one were the Grilled Pork Chop.

They have nice mixed drinks, wine selection, liquor choice, and beers. They also have a great pasta dish selection, and I will try one the next time we come back.

For entrees we had the Faroe Island Salmon, the Grilled Pork Chop, and the Filet Mignon topped with Cacio E Pepe Raviolo which you must taste. Another favorite from Isaac is the Roasted Branzino.

I highly recommend Bad Roman, a big shoutout to all their employees who work extremely hard and will be back again. Bad Roman will be one of the restaurants I recommend when asked for a special place to go if you want to have a wonderful time.

text.text:
During the Road Scholar's "American Mosaic - An NYC Exploration" program from Jun 22 to Jun 27, 2025, we had one dinner and five breakfasts at Tick Tock Diner located inside the New Yorker Hotel. Access was through its indoor entrance located next to the "Butcher & Banker" entrance, which was located to the left of the hotel's elevator hall. Since we were part of a tour group, we got vouchers that listed what we could order. No standard menus for us.

The sole exception was Day 1 dinner. We relied on an oral menu recited by the waiter. Since I don't have a photographic memory, I asked him to repeat the entrees. For appetizers, I had chicken noodle soup, and wife had salad; for entrees, I had steak (medium rare) with onion rings, Wife had grilled chicken with veggies. The chicken noodle soup was salty, easily the saltiest chicken noodle soup I ever tasted. It was also the smallest in portion size, slightly larger than a Chinese tea cup. As for the entree, the steak was slightly bigger than my hand, and served well-done instead of medium rare. I did not see any red inside the meat. The onion rings tasted like they came straight from the fryer and without any seasonings. The ones at Burger King tasted better. Wife remarked that her chicken looked pan-fried than grilled. Dessert was a scoop of vanilla ice cream with chocolate syrup, which wasn't bad. Clearly, Tick Tock's specialty is breakfast, not dinner. Rating: 2.5/5.

For Day 2 breakfast, I had (scrambled) eggs with hash browns, two sausages and two slices of toast. (The vouchers called the hash browns "potatoes".) Wife had waffles with two sausages. According to her, the waffles tasted like flour and eggs than real waffles. For beverage, everyone was provided with a tall glass of water and a small glass of orange juice. The waiter misunderstood the order for coffee and brought two cups when we specifically requested one. Since Wife didn't drink coffee, that extra cup was mine. My order had a generous portion size, so much so that I still felt full at lunchtime. Like Day 1's dinner, the food was served plain without any seasonings, giving a bland taste. Thankfully, excess pepper compensated for that. Comparatively speaking, IHOP's version of the order was better. However, it was good enough for me to order it again for Day 6 breakfast. Score: 3/5

For Day 3 breakfast, I had Greek omelet with hash browns and tea. The omelet had tomatoes and sour cheese. The portion size was almost as large as Day 2 breakfast's order. I didn't like the strong taste of sour cheese, which made this the worst of the breakfast experiences. Score: 2.5/5

For Day 4 breakfast, I had western omelet with hash browns and tea. It was served at the same portion size as Day 3's Greek omelet but with more ingredients - such as bell peppers, onions and ham – and tastier. It was the best of the breakfast orders, so much so that I ordered it again for Day 5 breakfast. Score: 4/5

Of the four entrees, eggs with hash browns, sausages and toasts had the largest portion size, while steak with onion rings had the smallest. In terms of taste, western omelet was the best and Greek omelet was the worst. Service was consistently good, and the booths had sufficient legroom and comfort. Every time we were there, the TVs were set to local news but the muted sound level was conducive to making ourselves heard. Tick Tock was never crowded during all our visits. In all the breakfast visits, we showed up before 8am and were immediately escorted to our tables. Not once did we ever had to wait.

I'm glad that all the meals were covered by the tour program. If it was up to me, I wouldn't visit Tick Tock Diner, or wouldn't come back after the first visit. For what it was worth, it was alright.

My sister and I visited the Brooklyn Chophouse Times Square location to celebrate our birthdays and watch the Knicks win the NBA Championship, and while the food and atmosphere were excellent, the service started off as one of the worst dining experiences I’ve had.

We arrived around 6:45 PM, and the restaurant wasn’t very busy until about 8:00 PM. We started with the lobster wonton soup, which was absolutely amazing and packed with flavor. Next came the oxtail bao buns—the meat was tender and flavorful, and the soft bao bun was the perfect complement. I also enjoyed the Caesar salad, which had just the right amount of dressing for my taste.

Unfortunately, our experience with our initial server, Jay (or Jashawn, I’m not exactly sure), left a lot to be desired. It took nearly 15 minutes before he even acknowledged our table to take a drink order. Throughout the evening, he seemed more focused on his phone and catering to his regular customers than providing attentive service to all guests. His approach felt very nonchalant and lacked the level of care I’d expect from a restaurant at this price point.

Since we were celebrating our birthdays, I asked if there were any birthday specials. His response was, “No, but I can bring you some shots.” We ordered them, but after waiting 25 minutes with no sign of the shots, I had to speak with the hostess for the second time regarding the lack of service. The blonde hostess was phenomenal—professional, accommodating, and genuinely concerned about making things right. Once she got involved, the shots arrived almost immediately.

Thankfully, management reassigned us to a new server who completely turned the experience around. He was attentive, checked on us at appropriate times, and delivered the level of hospitality I was expecting when I first walked in. He cleaned up what had become a very frustrating situation and helped salvage our birthday celebration.

To finish the evening, we ordered dessert, and our new server surprised us with apple wontons topped with a sparkler to celebrate our birthdays. It was a thoughtful touch that made the night feel special.

The kitchen deserves a tremendous amount of credit because every dish we ordered was excellent. The food was consistently delicious, and I enjoyed watching the NBA Finals in the restaurant’s atmosphere. However, first impressions matter, and at a restaurant where an automatic 18% gratuity is added to every bill, the service should consistently match the quality of the food.

If you’re planning to visit Brooklyn Chophouse Times Square, I highly recommend the food and atmosphere. The kitchen did a phenomenal job. Just hope you don’t get Jay as your server. Thankfully, the hostess and our replacement waiter stepped up and transformed what was shaping up to be a disappointing experience into one worth remembering.

text.text: You can't beat the convenience of the location.   Between a theater and a parking lot in midtown is magical ✨️.       My first thoughts upon entering the location was "this place is nice."  That sentiment was quickly followed by "this place is dark. "  perhaps they are conserving energy 🤔 but it was not swanky or romantic dark,  it was dark!  Even the bathroom was dark.  Other guests on both sides of our table complained about the same thing.  We ordered small plates and a chicken 🐔 soup thingy.   The shrimp and the lobster wonton were good.   The ribs were possibly undercooked buy definitely tough and pulling back.   I could not see if they were raw-ish because it was too dark.   The service,  or lack of service was striking.   The place was not crowded at all.   After being seated we waited about 10 minutes for the server to approach us.  She apologized for the wait and offered that she was having a conversation that she could not break away from. WHAT!  Even the water 💧 took a looooog time to be poured.   My friend ordered bread 🍞 for his soup 3 times.   That NEVER arrived.   There seemed like there was no urgency at all on the part of anyone that worked there.  Keep in mind that this was before curtain time on Broadway.   Once we got our bill, which was reasonably priced,  we had to get up and walk towards the door at 7:55 in order to get attention so that we could pay.  Not a bad experience but certainly not one to rave about.   Your mileage may vary.

Estiatorio Milos Midtown
125 W 55th st, NY N Y 10019

My wife & I were in the neighborhood for show & decided this would be just the right restaurant for our evening out.
We made reservations for 5:30 but arrived at 5:00.
The hostess happily showed us to our seats- smack center in the restaurant.
Milos is a beautiful restaurant and has a fresh upscale feel.
We knew we were on a tight schedule so we already had our dinner pre selected- to save time.
We were ordering off the Pre-fixe theater menu- something i've never done before- and may not do again.
For the sake of saving money, and or time- perhaps...its a good idea but I personally didn't feel comfortable- or at ease ordering this way- I felt like the portions didn't quite live up to expectations.
We ordered Lychee Martinis- they came out very strong.
We returned them for a house Cab & a Mezcal Margarita which were both very good.
We ordered  the whole grilled Dorado & The lobster pasta. I can happily report- both were delicious.
Id definitely go back, but perhaps to the other location just to mix it up a bit.
I do recommend.

Milos in Midtown is an experience. The moment you walk in, the pristine ice display of whole fish and giant lobster sets the tone: this place is about ultra-fresh seafood, simply prepared. The lunch special is still one of the better deals in Midtown-$40 or so for a three-course meal featuring their famous Greek spread, fried zucchini, and a generous piece of grilled fish. Dinner is another story entirely, with prices that can easily hit $150+ per person before drinks.
The standout for me is the Atlantic lobster (appetizer-sized, but huge) and the grilled Mediterranean sea bass, which is filleted tableside. The saganaki cheese is theatrically flambéed, and the olive oil is so good you'll want to drink it. Service is polished and professional, though it can feel rushed during peak hours.

Evening well spent.

text.text: The Capital Grille in Midtown is where I go when I need a reliable business dinner that never disappoints. The dry-aged porterhouse is consistently excellent with a deep beefy flavor that comes from proper aging and a kitchen that respects the process. The lobster mac and cheese is indulgent in the best way creamy rich with chunks of lobster that justify the price. The wine list is extensive and well-curated with an emphasis on bold California cabs that pair perfectly with the steaks. What sets Capital Grille apart from the trendy steakhouse scene is consistency. Every single time I walk in I know exactly what I am getting and it is always good. The service is professional without being robotic they know their regulars and they treat first-timers with the same attention. The bar area is ideal for a pre-dinner drink or a meeting that does not need a full table. The decor is classic dark wood and white tablecloths but it never feels dated it feels intentional. In a city where restaurants come and go faster than taxi cabs Capital Grille has maintained its standard year after year. That reliability might not make headlines but it builds a loyal clientele and I am one of them. When the deal matters and the dinner needs to be right this is where I go. It never lets me down.

text.text: Today was my first time at Hillstone and the food truly made the experience unforgettable. My friend and I had a fabulous time enjoying our meal while having a lovely conversation. The steak was cooked perfectly with so much flavor in every bite, and the chicken salad was fresh, bright, and incredibly satisfying. Every dish tasted thoughtful and high quality. You can tell the kitchen takes real pride in what they serve. I absolutely love this place and I am already looking forward to coming back.

text.text:
Can I go back again really soon??!!! Wonderful atmosphere with cozy, elevated vibes. The service was spot on- our waitress had a friendly attitude, great menu suggestions and knows just when to check in. Cocktails- who doesn’t want their drink to stay cold? I do, and that happens here with cold glass replacements. The food was delicious. The menu has so many options. Our choices the night we visited were- the sushi (coconut roll and pressed). What a great start! Our entrees were the trout (so underrated) perfectly seasoned and the Hawaiian steak (med-rare) that was done perfectly and melted in your mouth. The sides we chose were the potatoes colcannon (mashed potatoes mixed with cabbage and kale) which were so creamy and broccoli nicely seasoned with butter and Parmesan. The slaw that came with the trout was delicious and not boring.
This restaurant is definitely a repeat for sure!

text.text:
My bestie told me about this place when she found on TikTok and we made reservations on 11/22 for 12/22 at 4:30pm. There were reservations in between throughout the month but it was too early for our liking 11-2pm mostly. I didn't know there was a dress code but I'm glad they sent notice ahead of time. We both went in jeans with boots and bodysuits, comfy and cute yet presentable. This restaurant is def casual with an upscale vibe.

My bestie had a drink & i had a Coke. We both got salads mine was the grilled chicken Caesar salad and hers was a tuna tartar both excellent. The croutons & chicken were to die for. My bestie then had roast beef with fries and i had the s almon with broccoli. The star of the show was that salmon wow wow wow! Made to perfection and the light sauce on it was excellent! My bestie was even amazed and she's not a salmon person. I left no crumbs on the salad or salmon haha. For dessert we shared the brownie with a scoop of ice cream and it was delicious!! Def for anyone allergic to nuts but wow the nuts made the dessert so good.

Lastly, service was amazing ! The servers were so nice, professional and personable. Bathrooms were clean and the restaurant at nice location right next to the 6 train. I can't wait to come back with my husband ! He's going to love this spot!

Definitely a legendary spot worth visiting, but make sure to book in advance, it fills up quickly.

text.text: Amazing experience, but for a 2 Star Michelin, it needs some improvement! I was expecting something more intimate and the restaurant was packed. We were seated in a table with a long couch with two other families very close to us. We had the six course omnivore and two courses were disappointing: the caviar taste disappeared in the green garbanzo beans; the wagyu per se was tasteless and needs improvement! The last thing was the restroom, which was very basic and not compatible with the restaurant sophistication!
